summary: Arabic chooses the negator by sentence type and tense. A present verb is negated with لَا: لَا أُحِبُّ الْبَصَلَ. A sentence without a verb (“is not”, “is not here”, “does not have”) is negated with لَيْسَ — a verb with past-tense endings but present meaning, which agrees with the subject (لَسْتُ، لَيْسَتْ …) and puts a noun or adjective predicate in the accusative: هٰذِهِ لَيْسَتْ جَزَرَةً; لَيْسَ عِنْدِي ثُومٌ. The past is negated with لَمْ + jussive (لَمْ آكُلْ), the future with لَنْ + subjunctive (لَنْ آكُلَ); مَا + past verb is classical and dialectal. The answer “no” is also لَا.

askYourself: Is there a present verb? → لَا directly before it; the verb stays indicative (-u).
Is it a sentence without a verb (X is Y / X is here / I have)? → لَيْسَ, agreeing with the subject.
After لَيْسَ, is the predicate a noun or an adjective? → accusative (جَزَرَةً، جَائِعًا).
Is it past or future? → لَمْ + jussive / لَنْ + subjunctive — not لَا.
Is it the answer “no”? → لَا on its own, then a comma.

traps: *لَا هٰذِهِ جَزَرَةٌ is wrong: use لَيْسَ — هٰذِهِ لَيْسَتْ جَزَرَةً.
لَيْسَ looks like a past verb but means the present: لَسْتُ جَائِعًا = I am not hungry.
Do not negate a past verb with لَا: “I didn’t eat” = لَمْ آكُلْ.
لَا “no” and لَا “not” are written the same; the answer is followed by a pause or comma: لَا، شُكْرًا.
